newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - British Telecom down.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - British Telecom down.

text.p: Shares of British Telecommunications Plc were down in U.S. trading after news the company was in merger talks with with MCI Communications Corp.
British Telecom shares were down 1-5/8 at 56 on the New York Stock Exchange, off a low of 55-7/8.

"They definitely have to go out of their home country," said Scott Wright, who follows British Telecom for Argus Research. "I have a feeling (the deal) will be based around the internet where MCI has been focusing and where the real growth in the U.S. market is."
Elsewhere, British Petroleum Co Plc was down three at 125-3/8 in U.S. trading while Royal Dutch Petroleum fell was down 2-3/8.
Lower crude prices and lingering disappointment over Royal Dutch/Shell Group results depressed oil stocks on the London Stock Exchange this morning.
Mexican stocks traded in New York were mostly steady after Oppenheimer & Co raised its weighting on Mexico to overweight from underweight.

Vinod Seghal, Oppenheimer's director of research for Latin America, said that Mexican stocks could rally 15 to 20 percent in the coming weeks and that short-term interest rates could decline to 25 percent from Thursday's high of 31 percent.
He said that downside stock market risk was five percent.
Among today's special situations, Oppenheimer cut its rating on on Phamis Inc to accumulate from buy based on near term concerns. The stock was down 3-3/8 at 11-5/8.
Shares of Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd were up 13/16 at 42-11/16 in Nasdaq trading.
Teva said Friday that the Food and Drug Administration has given it approval to make and sell 2.5 mg Indapamide tablets.
The tablets are a generic equivalent of a Lozol, a drug made by Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc to treat hypertension, the company said.
